title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 11
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 11: casting bread on the waters, sowing in the morning, the sweetness of light, and rejoicing in youth.

questions.text: What does the opening verse say will happen if you cast your bread on the waters?
questions.explanation: Cast your bread on the waters, for you shall find it after many days.

answers.text: It will feed the fish of the sea
It will be carried away forever
You shall find it after many days
The waters will return it the same day

questions.text: To how many should you give a portion, because you don't know what evil will be on the earth?
questions.explanation: Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight, for you don't know what evil will be on the earth.

answers.text: To seven, yes, even to eight
To three, yes, even to four
To ten, yes, even to twelve

questions.text: According to this chapter, what happens in the place where a tree falls?
questions.explanation: If a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there shall it be.

questions.text: What will he who observes the wind not do?
questions.explanation: He who observes the wind won't sow, and he who regards the clouds won't reap.

questions.text: Just as you don't know the way of the wind, what else does this chapter say you don't know?
questions.explanation: As you don't know the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, so you don't know the work of God who does all.

answers.text: The work of God who does all

questions.text: Why should you sow your seed in the morning and not withhold your hand in the evening?
questions.explanation: You don't know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.

answers.text: Because the days of harvest are short
Because rain is coming on the earth
Because you don't know which will prosper
Because the idle man stays poor

questions.text: What does this chapter call sweet and pleasant for the eyes?
questions.explanation: Truly the light is sweet, and it is a pleasant thing for the eyes to see the sun.

answers.text: The light, and seeing the sun

questions.text: If a man lives many years and rejoices in them all, what should he still remember?
questions.explanation: Let him remember the days of darkness, for they shall be many; all that comes is vanity.

questions.text: The young man is told to rejoice in his youth, but what must he know?
questions.explanation: The young man may walk in the ways of his heart, but must know that for all these things God will bring him into judgment.

answers.text: That his youth will pass away like the morning dawn
That his own heart will surely deceive him in the end
That for all these things God will bring him into judgment
That the days of darkness are drawing near to him

questions.text: What does the last verse of the chapter say about youth and the dawn of life?
questions.explanation: Remove sorrow from your heart and put away evil from your flesh, for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.

answers.text: They are a gift that lasts
They are better than old age
